prompt.text: A page's memory keeps growing after you close a panel. What is likely?

hints: Something is still holding on after it should be free.
cards.fullLine: Memory that keeps growing after you close a panel suggests a memory leak.

prompt.text: Elements removed from the page but still held in JavaScript are

answer.text: Elements removed from the page but still held in JavaScript are detached nodes.

hints: They are no longer part of the tree.
cards.fullLine: Elements removed from the page but still held in JavaScript are detached nodes.

teaching.text: The page no longer shows it, but script may still hold a reference.

teaching.alt: A page tree with one node cut away, still tied by a line to a script variable

teaching.search: How To Detect Memory Leaks In Your Web App
teaching.alt: Finding memory leaks with browser developer tools

cards.summary: A live reference keeps a node

prompt.text: Which keeps a detached element alive?

hints: Somewhere in script, a variable still points at it.
cards.fullLine: A live JavaScript reference keeps a detached element alive.

prompt.text: Which DevTools panel takes heap snapshots?

hints: Its name is what is being measured.
cards.fullLine: The Memory panel takes heap snapshots.

teaching.text: It records what the heap holds at one moment.

cards.summary: A closure can hold an object

prompt.text: that captures a large object can keep it alive.

answer.text: A closure that captures a large object can keep it alive.

hints: It is a function that remembers its outer variables.
cards.fullLine: A closure that captures a large object can keep it alive.

teaching.text: A function can keep outer variables alive after their scope ends.

prompt.text: Which structure lets a key be collected when nothing else holds it?

hints: Its first word says how firmly it holds anything.
cards.fullLine: A WeakMap lets a key be collected when nothing else holds it.

prompt.text: When nothing references an object, the garbage

answer.text: When nothing references an object, the garbage collector may reclaim it.

hints: It tidies what nobody points at.
cards.fullLine: When nothing references an object, the garbage collector may reclaim it.

teaching.text: Unused objects are reclaimed automatically when nothing points to them.

cards.summary: A rising heap suggests a reference

prompt.text: A heap snapshot taken after the same action shows memory only rising. What does that suggest?

hints: If the count falls back, the claim is safe.
cards.fullLine: A heap that only rises after the same action suggests something is still referenced.

prompt.text: A listener added on every render without removal is a common

answer.text: A listener added on every render without removal is a common leak.

hints: The heap grows with each new copy.
cards.fullLine: A listener added on every render without removal is a common leak.

teaching.text: Every render adds another one, and none are removed.

prompt.text: Which recording shows what creates memory while an action runs?

hints: It plots creation over time, not just a final total.
cards.fullLine: Recording an allocation timeline shows what creates memory while an action runs.
